Rumour-to-Relief recorded runs · replayed offline

A monsoon flash flood in Kullu, Himachal Pradesh. Villagers, panchayat officials, WhatsApp-style rumour amplifiers and the district disaster office talk through small open-weight models through Otari: a self-hosted gateway for the local model families, and otari.ai for the hosted ones. Does the model that drives the agents change which intervention looks best?

    Ranked by at-risk villagers evacuated, ties broken by fewer caught. One seed per cell: two live runs of the same cell differ by about 6 points from model sampling alone, so gaps that size are noise.

    Otari usage, selected run (recorded live)

    Recorded runs, replayed offline. Every model call in these runs went live through Otari. The local families ran on a self-hosted gateway with one virtual key per cohort, per-run token budgets, a routing policy per family and a misinformation guardrail on every interpretation. The hosted families ran on otari.ai, where the district office also closes each run with a report computed by Otari's code-execution tool. The page replays those answers call for call, so no gateway is needed to view it.

    Movement and belief rules are hand-written and calibrated only against plausibility targets for the official warning channel; costs are notional prices on local models, not charges. Map data © OpenStreetMap contributors. Generated .
